The score rates a night on the measurable dimensions of sleep health (Buysse 2014): how long, how unbroken, how regular and when you slept.

# Graded, not pass or fail
Every measure is graded around its published threshold. Just meeting the threshold earns 60 % of its points; better values earn more, up to full points at an excellent value. A night that just meets every criterion scores about 80, so the score still separates good nights from very good ones.

# The parts
- Duration, 40 points: time asleep against your need, your usual sleep kept between 7 and 9 hours. Full points at your need, 60 % at 85 % of it, none at 60 %.
- Continuity, 25 points: the National Sleep Foundation's quality criteria as thresholds. Sleep efficiency 85 % (excellent 95 %), awake after falling asleep 20 minutes (excellent 5), time to fall asleep 30 minutes (excellent 10), one long awakening of 5 minutes or more (excellent none).
- Regularity, 25 points: the middle of the night against your usual over the last two weeks. Excellent within 10 minutes, threshold 45 minutes, nothing beyond two hours. Irregular sleep predicts mortality more strongly than short sleep (Windred 2024).
- Timing, 10 points: the middle of the night between 02:00 and 04:00, the sleep health criterion. 60 % an hour outside it, nothing beyond two and a half hours.

# What is not scored
- Sleep stages: wrist sensors tell them apart only roughly, and one night's shares say little about its quality.
- Brief arousals: they are a normal part of healthy sleep.

# Ratings
- 80 and above: good
- 65 to 79: fair
- Below 65: poor

# Compared with Fitbit
Fitbit's score also counts deep and REM sleep, restlessness and sleeping heart rate, with weights it does not publish, so the two can differ by 10 points or more. Resting heart rate and HRV count in readiness instead.

The stages as your watch estimated them from movement and heart rate, one lane per stage.

- Deep sleep: the most restorative stage, mostly early in the night.
- REM sleep: dreaming sleep, longer towards the morning.
- Light sleep: about half of a normal night.
- Awake: short awakenings are normal; several a night are part of healthy sleep.

The line under the headline names what held the night back most: the measures below their threshold, or, on a good night, the ones furthest from excellent.

How the night compares with published ranges. The tinted band on each bar is the range, the dot the night.

- Time to fall asleep, awake after falling asleep, long awakenings and sleep efficiency: the National Sleep Foundation's sleep quality recommendations (Ohayon 2017).
- Deep and REM sleep: typical shares for healthy adults. Compared with a sleep lab, wrist sensors misplace a good part of stage time, so these two are shown but not scored.

Heart rate during the sleep, averaged over five minutes and smoothed over a quarter of an hour, so that turning over or a brief awakening does not dominate the line.

- Average: the mean over the whole night.
- Lowest: the calmest quarter of an hour.
- Resting: the resting heart rate your watch derived from the night, drawn as a line.

Heart rate usually falls through the first half of the night. A night that stays well above your usual, or does not fall, often follows hard training late in the day, alcohol, a big late meal or the start of an illness.

Measured while you slept and compared with your own normal.

- HRV: the median of the watch's five-minute values, as Fitbit reports it. The normal range is your 60-day average plus or minus half a standard deviation, in place once there are 14 nights.
- Resting heart rate: as your watch derived it from the night. Usual is the average of the last 30 nights.
- Breathing rate: breaths per minute during sleep. A clear rise above usual is a common early sign of illness.

The last 7 or 30 nights up to the night shown, with the average beside each chart. Tinted bands are the healthy range: a good score, your sleep need, 85 % efficiency and the typical deep and REM shares.\n\nBed and wake times show one bar per night from going to bed to getting up; bars that line up mean a regular rhythm.
